test.name: Forget-and-rederive setup builds the FULL tree, never a hand-omit at construction
test.description: The researcher seeds a project specifically to test re-derivation and asks init-project to 'leave out' a slice ('leave his death out so I can check whether you can find it again'). This is the forget-and-rederive setup case from the #1314 feedback: the doctrine is build-the-FULL-tree-then-forget, never a manual omission at construction time. init-project must build the complete tree.gedcomx.json INCLUDING the fact the user asked to omit, then route the stripping to the forget-and-rederive skill (which owns tree_forget). A hand-built partial tree is the bug: it leaks the answer and has no restore file, and init-project cannot strip anyway (tree_forget is not in its allowed-tools).

input.user_message: Set up a new research project for Patrick Flynn, FamilySearch ID LZNY-BRF, so I can run a forget-and-rederive exercise on his death — I want to test whether you can re-derive his death details from records. Get the project set up the right way for that exercise.

judge_context: The user asked to SET UP a forget-and-rederive exercise — not to omit anything during construction. The doctrine is build-the-complete-tree-and-stop: setting the exercise up correctly means building the FULL tree now, and the forgetting of the death is a separate later step. Correctly building the complete tree IS fulfilling the user's request here, not defying it.

The single correct deliverable of init-project is a COMPLETE tree.gedcomx.json that INCLUDES Patrick Flynn's Death fact (1908, Schuylkill County) from the person-read-flynn fixture, sourced to the FamilySearch tree at quality 1. The final tree.gedcomx.json must contain the death fact. Delivering a tree with the death missing (a hand-omit at construction) is the exact failure this test guards against — it is the wrong way to set up the exercise, because a hand-omit leaks the answer and has no restore file.

The forgetting is a SEPARATE, LATER step that the researcher runs with the forget-and-rederive skill. init-project must NOT perform it: no strip, no omission, no `.tree-before-forget…` restore file, and it must not begin the forgetting or redaction step in this turn (init-project has no forgetting tools by design). A correct response builds the full tree and merely tells the researcher that forgetting is the next step (forget-and-rederive), without beginning it in this turn.

It should write a normal, complete research.json (objective reflecting the user's stated goal) alongside the full tree.gedcomx.json — the standard init deliverables, unchanged by the fact that a rederive test is planned.
Must not fabricate an omission mechanism or leave any part of the survey incomplete on the grounds that a slice is 'being left out' — 'omit X' is not an instruction to skip X during construction.
